name: Queen Ethelburga's Collegiate
tagline: A co-educational UK boarding school between York, Leeds and Harrogate, with a dedicated international department.
summary: Queen Ethelburga's is a 220-acre campus in North Yorkshire with day and boarding students from over 40 nationalities (about 40% of the community is international). International students board in the same houses as UK students and can join from Year 3 through Year 13, or take the one-year NCUK International Foundation Year. English-language programmes run alongside GCSE, A Level and BTEC study.
year_groups: Year 3 to Year 13, plus International Foundation Year (age 17+)

notes: International students live in the same boarding houses as UK students.
Sixth Form boarders live in the Atrium, a university-style building with private bedrooms around the dining hall.
Younger boarders have dedicated dormitories; boarding rooms for the youngest students won a BSA refurbishment award in 2024.
International students can stay at school over every half-term and Easter holiday (organised activities and trips).
On-site medical centre and 24/7 campus security.

fees.deposit: Refundable; equal to one term's full fees
notes: Fees include VAT where applicable.
The registration fee is non-refundable and payable by bank transfer.
The source lists the same termly fee for Year 3 to Year 13.
fees.payment: Online bank transfer via Convera GlobalPay (140+ currencies)

admissions.intake: September (January also for the English Language Programme, Years 10-12). Applications are accepted year-round.
documents: Two copies of the most recent full school reports
steps: Register your interest (online form, or via an international representative or agent).
Send the application form and documents.
Take the online English test and CAT4 (an invigilator is needed; the school arranges this with your school, agent or test centre).
Complete the personal resume and interview.
Receive an offer letter stating the course, start date and fee.
Accept by completing the registration form and paying the registration fee and deposit.

entry_routes.programme: Key Stage 3 with EAL classes (King's Magna)
Two-year A Level / BTEC with IELTS/EAL lessons
entry_routes.requirement: IELTS 6 (GCSE grade 7+ for some A Levels)

entry_routes.programme: NCUK International Foundation Year (Business or Science)

admissions.note: The school states there are no formal entry requirements for international students beyond a basic level of English.

facilities: Muggles activity centre (gaming suite, climbing wall, padel court)
highlights: QEGUK Gold Award in International Student Provision
ISI inspection (October 2023) praised specialist EAL support
NCUK International Foundation Year (Business or Science pathway)
International summer school in July (2, 3 or 4 weeks)

name: Ashbourne College
tagline: A selective private GCSE and A level college in Kensington, London, with classes of ten or fewer. Day college: no boarding.
summary: Ashbourne is a small, independently owned college next to Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park, founded in 1981. It teaches GCSEs (Years 10 and 11) and A levels (Years 12 and 13) in classes typically capped at ten, with a weekly personal tutor for each student and a university-style, first-name atmosphere (there is no uniform). Ashbourne is not a boarding school: international students live in hostels, student residences or homestays that the college lists but does not inspect, and students living outside the UK need a UK education guardian.
year_groups: Year 10 to Year 13 (GCSE and A level)

accommodation.summary: No on-site accommodation: Ashbourne is not a boarding school.
notes: The college keeps a list of accommodation providers (student hostels and residences, and homestays with selected families) that students apply to independently.
About 75 students currently live in these arrangements, split roughly evenly between hostels and homestays.
Typical prices are GBP 100 to 700 per week, from shared rooms to self-contained studios, 10 to 30 minutes' journey from the college.
Ashbourne does not inspect these properties or guarantee their standard or safety; families should carry out their own checks.
accommodation.guardianship: Parents of students living outside the UK must appoint a UK-based education guardian with legal authority to act on their behalf (medical care, travel, day-to-day support). The college can provide a list of guardianship and accommodation providers; we can request it for you.

english_support: English language (IELTS) programme: 2 hours a week from Year 12

results.label: A level progress ranking (value added), England

notes: International student fee shown (A level and GCSE). Home students pay GBP 13,500 per term. All fees include VAT.
Accommodation is not included and not provided by the college.
Exam fees: GBP 350 per subject (AS and A2), GBP 160 per GCSE subject.
Practical fees: GBP 300 per subject per term (Fine Art, Graphics, Textiles, Music, Drama and science subjects). UCAS fee GBP 65 (Year 13). Individual tuition GBP 120 per hour.
Student visa application fee GBP 348 from outside the UK (paid to the UK government, plus the Immigration Healthcare Surcharge).

admissions.intake: September (also a January intake for new students). Rolling admissions year-round. Scholarship cycles close with an offer by 1 Dec (largest scholarships), 1 Mar (partial) and 1 Jun (none).
assessments: Interview with the Principal, Director of Studies or a senior member of staff
Art subjects: portfolio of work may be requested
documents: Last two sets of academic reports
GCSE grades or predicted grades (or equivalent)
Copy of passport (and UK visa page if the student already has one)
steps: Submit your documents (school report, passport copy and personal statement).
Sit the in-house admissions tests, scheduled at a mutually convenient time.
Attend an interview (some applicants are invited to a second one).
Receive the outcome, usually within a week of the interview; successful applicants typically have two weeks to accept.
International students: Ashbourne issues a CAS (Certificate of Acceptance for Studies) once fees are settled and documents are checked, then you apply for a Child Student or Student visa.

entry_routes.programme: Two-year GCSE programme (core subjects in Year 10, options in Year 11)

entry_routes.requirement: Typically grade 6 or above across GCSEs; IELTS 5.0 (CEFR B1) for the Student visa

admissions.note: Ashbourne is selective but assesses each application individually; it is free to apply.

highlights: Rated Outstanding by Ofsted in December 2021 and November 2024
Classes typically capped at ten; weekly one-to-one personal tutor and a dedicated UCAS tutor in Year 13
25+ A level subjects plus Oxbridge, medicine, engineering, finance and natural sciences programmes
Ranked in the top 2.5% of schools and colleges in England for A level progress (2023/24)
Located beside Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park

name: St Clare's, Oxford (IB)
tagline: England's oldest IB World School: the IB Diploma and a one-to-three-term Pre-IB in North Oxford, with boarding and day places and classes averaging nine students.
summary: St Clare's, Oxford teaches the two-year IB Diploma (ages 16 to 19) and a Pre-IB bridging programme (ages 15 to 16) on a campus of Victorian and Edwardian buildings on the Banbury Road, 1.5 km from Oxford city centre. Students board in 12 houses near the campus, or attend as day students; day students eat with boarders and join every trip and activity. The school is semi-selective, welcomes more than 50 nationalities and has been delivering international education for over 70 years. This record covers the IB school only, not the college's summer, adult or teacher-training courses.
year_groups: Pre-IB (age 15-16) and the two-year IB Diploma (age 16-19)

notes: 12 boarding houses near the campus, typically 16 to 18 students each, every house with a House Parent.
Single, twin and triple rooms; over half of the rooms are en suite. Most boarders share with a student from another country.
Breakfast, lunch and dinner every day, all dietary requirements catered for; house kitchens for snacks.
Weekly boarding exists for a small number of students and is only open to those living in England or Wales (same fee as full boarding).
Day students join boarders for all meals (included in the fee), have lockers and a student hub, and take part in all trips and activities.
All Pre-IB and IB students on a Child Student visa whose parents live overseas must have a nominated UK Educational Guardian.
The college is closed to students during half-term and school holidays (set departure and arrival days apply).

english_support: Pre-IB: tiered English classes and EAL support
IB Diploma: Language B English with EAL support (English guide level B2 mid, not a minimum)

results.label: IB Diploma average points (2026 cohort of 123; world average 31)
Students scoring above the world average

fees.deposit: IB Diploma enrolment deposit GBP 3,500. Pre-IB deposit: GBP 1,400 (autumn or spring entry), GBP 700 (summer), GBP 3,500 (full year).

tiers.label: Boarding
tiers.note: Paid in two instalments of GBP 33,092: due 13 August 2026 and 13 December 2026.

tiers.label: Day
tiers.note: Paid in two instalments of GBP 15,493: due 13 August 2026 and 13 December 2026.

notes: Totals include 20% VAT. Exam fees, book fees (except Foreign Language Literature) and travel and fees insurance are included and VAT-exempt.
Term fees differ by term, so the headline is the full-year fee. Compare with other schools on the yearly cost.

Extras: Duke of Edinburgh's Award (Bronze compulsory for Pre-IB, GBP 210-315; Gold optional, GBP 580-685); field trips for Biology (GBP 820-945), Geography (GBP 290-315) and ESS (GBP 60-65) students; Pre-IB activities up to GBP 315 a term.
Other costs: private music lessons GBP 35-70 each, art materials GBP 160 for two years (Visual Arts), calculator GBP 120-160, airport transfers GBP 190-305, SEN or learning support varies.
fees.payment: Flywire for international payments (home currency, card or bank transfer), or UK bank transfer; cash accepted up to GBP 250.

admissions.intake: IB Diploma starts in September. Pre-IB starts in September, January or April and lasts one, two or three terms.
assessments: English and Maths placement test (decides Standard or Higher Level courses)
Interview with the Vice Principal or another senior member of staff (in person or online)
documents: School reports or academic transcripts for the last two years (SSAT scores accepted from the USA)
Official transcripts in English or with a certified translation
Online application form and registration fee
steps: Your K12 Onboard adviser contacts the school's admissions team.
Send school reports or transcripts for the last two years; if satisfactory you receive the online application form.
Complete the application form and pay the registration fee.
Visit and interview with the Vice Principal or a senior member of staff (online with a 360 virtual tour if you cannot travel).
Receive a verbal offer after the interview, then written confirmation.

entry_routes.programme: Pre-IB, ages 15-16 (1, 2 or 3 terms; 15 students maximum; 30 lessons a week)
entry_routes.requirement: English guide level B1 mid-high (a guide, not a minimum)

entry_routes.programme: Two-year IB Diploma, ages 16-19 (six subjects plus Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS; 15 students maximum)
entry_routes.requirement: English guide level B2 mid (a guide, not a minimum); Maths and English placement tests

admissions.note: Semi-selective: decisions use previous academic results, the placement tests and an interview. Means-tested scholarships are open for 2027 entry: standard deadline 11 December 2026, assessment day 23 January 2027.

facilities: Campus of Victorian and Edwardian buildings on the Banbury Road, 1.5 km from Oxford city centre and about 50 km from London
Science laboratories, art studio and music studio
Dining hall and The Globe café
Accessible room and a non-denominational prayer room
Off-site sports venues: Oxford City FC, Ferry Leisure Centre, Smash Padel Oxford and others
highlights: 2026 IB average 36 points against a world average of 31; 13 students scored 43 to 45
School figure: 90% of students go to their first-choice university
Weekly personal tutoring, careers counselling and a leadership programme
Full and partial means-tested scholarships for the IB Diploma (day and boarding)

review_flags: Fees: the headline is the boarding full-year fee including VAT (GBP 66,185); day full-year is GBP 30,985. Term fees differ by term. The site's dollar prices use a fixed exchange rate and are not stored.
Nationalities are quoted as 'over 50', '50' and 'over 45' on different pages.
'90% of students score above the IB world average' appears on several pages; the 2026 results page says 80%. The 2026 average is 36 points; a three-year average of 35.3 is quoted elsewhere.
Campus is '25+' and '28' buildings on different pages. 'Oldest IB World School in England', 'nearly 50 years of IB expertise' and 'over 70 years' of school history refer to different things.
Ages 15-19 are inferred from Pre-IB (15-16) and the IB Diploma (16-19); the admissions FAQ says 16-18 for the Diploma.
Weekly boarding is only for students living in England or Wales, so it does not suit overseas families. The college closes to students at half-terms and holidays: check holiday care.

Not captured: gender mix, total student numbers, subject-by-subject IB options, and 64 linked PDFs (terms and conditions, accommodation, admissions and guardian policies). The general contact-us and homestay-providers pages were not scraped.
